newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Wallabies suffer heavy blow after Burke ruled out.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Wallabies suffer heavy blow after Burke ruled out.

text.p: Australia suffered a heavy blow ahead of next week's first rugby union test against France when fullback Matthew Burke was ruled out because of injury.
Burke has been sidelined with a groin injury and will be replaced by ACT Brumbies fullback Stephen Larkham for the game against the Five Nations champions in Sydney on June 21.

"Wallaby team doctor John Best advised coach Greg Smith that Matthew would be still unable to train for a few days and in the player's best interests, Matthew should be rested," team manager John McKay said in a statement on Friday.
No decision has yet been made on a replacement for Larkham on the Wallaby reserve bench, McKay said.
Burke sustained the injury while playing for New South Wales in the State of the Union match against Queensland in Brisbane last weekend.
Australia will host France in the second and final test in Brisbane on June 28.
